subject: Post-call: Lifespan hosting qualification & residency path
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@lifespan-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 15:14:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + immediate asks (Lifespan hosting qualification)

Alex — thanks again for taking time today. Quick written recap to make sure we captured the constraints and next steps. Please correct anything I missed.

Summary of what we heard (pain points & goals)
- Regulatory driver: Lifespan needs data residency in US (customer data and PHI must remain in-region).
- Preferred deployment: VPC peering / Direct Connect into a dedicated Redwood Dedicated pool; on-prem appliance is a contingency if procurement disallows cloud peering.
- Air-gap: not mandatory today but considered for high-risk datasets — procurement wants to understand the delta in scope/cost if air-gapped packaging is required.
- Security stack: Must provide SOC 2 Type II evidence, support for customer-managed KMS (Bring Your Own Key), audit logs with 90-day retention, and encryption-in-transit and at-rest.
- Network constraints: outbound egress via corporate proxy; strict firewall rules (only specific ports allowed); limited ability to open inbound ports to public IPs.
- Perf needs: steady-state ~50 req/s for inference, peeks to 150 req/s; p99 latency target <150ms for user-facing flows.

Decisions & asks from today
1) Lifespan to share current network diagram and proxy/firewall egress IPs (NetOps).
2) Redwood (Ben) to provide a one-page "VPC peering + Direct Connect" architecture with required ports and IP ranges and expected breakdown of changes vs. an air-gapped on-prem bundle.
3) Redwood (Monica) will compile the SOC2/KMS/audit-logs checklist and a short note on how KMS integration would work with customer-managed keys.
4) Procurement to confirm target procurement window (you mentioned end of Q3 but please confirm).

Attachments included in this thread: lifespan_network_v2.pdf (NetOps diagram you referenced), initial-scan-screenshot.png (my notes from the demo).

Proposed next touchpoints
- Technical sync (NetOps + Ben) — propose Thu Jun 10 11:00 AM PDT (I've added a tentative calendar invite)
- Security artifacts packet (Monica) delivered by Mon Jun 7

Please reply-all with any corrections. If the network diagram is sensitive, you can send it directly to monica.patel@redwoodinference.com.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Jasmine — that aligns with our notes. A couple clarifications from my side:
- We can support Direct Connect to AWS in us-west-2 or an equivalent private peering to GCP in us-west1; preference toward AWS.
- Air-gap would be restricted to a pilot initially (security wants a small subset of models/data). We're trying to avoid full air-gap due to Ops overhead, but need pricing delta.
- Procurement timeline: we are targeting an approved SOW by 2026-09-30; procurement will issue an RFx in August.

I'm attaching an updated network diagram (lifespan_network_v2.pdf) that includes our proxy egress details and the CIDR blocks we control. Ben / Monica, please use that as the source of truth for port/IP asks.

Hi all — quick technical constraints from NetOps so Redwood can bake into the architecture doc:
- Egress: all outbound must go through our BlueProxy cluster (10.8.0.0/22). No direct internet egress from host subnets.
- Peering: we will accept an AWS Transit Gateway attachment or a dedicated Direct Connect with private VIF. Peering over the public internet is not acceptable.
- Ports: Allow outbound 443, 8443, and outbound 53 (DNS). Inbound connections will only be accepted over the VPC peering path — no public-facing ELBs allowed.
- ACLs: We run tight ACLs; need finalized list of Redwood IP ranges that will terminate in our VPC so we can add whitelists.
- KMS: BYOK is acceptable via cross-account key policies; security will need a short integration plan and diagram.

If Redwood requires SFTP/S3 transfer for any air-gapped delivery, we will provide a signed S3 bucket with presigned uploads and an internal import job that runs behind our DMZ (this will require additional procurement approvals).

--
Lifespan NetOps
